species: rat (Wistar Kyoto; spontaneously hypertensive rat, SHR; Sprague-Dawley)
condition_other: ADHD (spontaneously hypertensive rat model; WKY and SD rats as controls)
readout_other: open-field test; modified Y-maze; Y-maze spontaneous alternation; DNMTP T-maze; spikes and LFP (16-channel electrode); Western blot for DAT and BDNF
direction_notes: In SHR rats TUS improved cognitive behaviour, raised neuronal firing rate and altered LFP band power and entropy, and increased BDNF by about 30%; WKY rats showed some changes too.

exposures.label: TUS to prefrontal cortex, 2 weeks daily

target.label: prefrontal cortex (1.25 mm left and right, 4.5 mm from bregma)

timing.protocol_description: 500 kHz, PRF 1 Hz, duty cycle 5%, stimulation duration 50 ms; stimulation performed continuously for 2 weeks for 15 min each time.

flags.reason: Paper calls the 50 ms value the 'stimulation duration'; recorded as the pulse duration because it equals duty cycle / PRF (5% of 1 s).

90 rats (30 per strain) are stated in total, split into TUS and control groups; the number exposed is not stated, so not computed.
Source text garbles the Isppa unit and the sentence ends with 'respectively'; value read as 9.36 W/cm2.
